title: Uncontrolled Key Space Divergence
pattern: Using local, uncoordinated auto-incrementing integer keys on separate database instances that are slated to be merged or synchronized during a system migration.
why_bad: It causes primary key collisions when importing or synchronizing records between the databases, forcing the migration team to write complex, slow, and fragile key translation logic [416].
detection: The use of database-native auto-increment fields (`SERIAL` or `AUTO_INCREMENT`) on databases that are target to merge, multi-leader replication, or cross-datacenter synchronization.
counterexample: Valid for strictly isolated, single-node databases that will never replicate or merge data with other instances.
fix: Use globally coordinated, collision-free key generation strategies, such as UUIDs/GUIDs, Snowflake IDs, or a centralized key allocator [194, 416, 664].
source: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, "Identity Field" [416]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 5 [194, 664]
